A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work despite the changed title, terminology, and organization. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support comparison, including matching retained experiments across renumbering and relocation.

before.justification: v1 reports original reconstruction experiments on LLFF, MipNeRF-360, Blender, and Neural 3D Video, together with ablations, loss-landscape analyses, and FreeNeRF experiments.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds RWP experiments, OMMO and DTU evaluations, sensitivity analyses, and additional reconstruction settings.

M1.justification: The principal per-Gaussian adaptive SAM procedure remains, including LoG-based scaling and weighted optimization. v2 Section 4.3 additionally describes adapting the perturbation magnitude and balance coefficient of the mixed-RWP objective. The renamed structure-aware method and idealized distance-map definition do not establish replacement of the retained LoG implementation.

E1.justification: v2 Appendix G adds evaluation on OMMO scene 15, targeting substantially larger outdoor scenes and depth ranges, and on DTU using AnySplat outputs for reconstruction refinement. The earlier LLFF, MipNeRF-360, Blender, and Neural 3D Video coverage remains. The additional LLFF view counts are protocol changes within retained coverage.

E2.justification: v2 adds SAM to the Blender lego comparison in Figure 1 and evaluates AnySplat without refinement versus standard and proposed 3DGS refinement in Table A7. Table 4 introduces an explicitly identified mixed-RWP comparison, while v1's RP/w/o-AP controls are no longer separately reported; their equivalence is not established. The five principal Table 1 baselines remain unchanged.

E3.justification: v2 adds LLFF evaluations with 2, 6, and 9 input views, a DTU post-optimization comparison, and wall-clock convergence measurements sampled every five seconds. Appendix D also reports fixing the Gaussian-mean radius multiplier to 1 instead of the earlier grid search; this does not establish that retained experiments were rerun. The main 3-view/12-view settings, downsampling, and metrics remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds regularization-weight sensitivity, LoG/DoH/distance-transform comparisons, input-view sensitivity, convergence-speed analysis, pixel-level loss-landscape probes, and an extrapolation failure case. It removes the isolated per-Gaussian normalization ablation, mean-radius sweep, and earlier random-perturbation study. Attribute-contribution and application-timing analyses are retained.

E5.justification: v1 Table 2 explicitly omits standard deviations, whereas v2 Table 2 supplies uncertainty values for retained ablation results. The stated ten LLFF runs and five MipNeRF-360 runs remain unchanged. There is no demonstrated increase in run counts or introduction of significance testing.

E6.justification: The main Table 1 scores and matched per-scene, FreeNeRF, and dynamic-scene results remain unchanged. Newly reported comparisons include LLFF PSNR of 20.079 versus 20.650 for RWP without/with the adaptation, and DTU PSNR of 13.239 versus 15.530 for standard/proposed post-optimization. Additional sensitivity and OMMO results appear, some earlier ablation entries disappear, and the application-timing AVGE curve changes numerically from Figure 10 to Figure A2.

T1.justification: v2 Section 3.2 and Appendix B introduce mathematical definitions of geometric tolerance and image-space/3D neighborhoods, then derive approximate image-variation and loss-variation bounds under ideal reconstruction, smoothness, and projection assumptions. These go beyond v1's intuitive frequency argument. The displayed SAM generalization theorem and discussion of its WSAM extension in v1 are removed.

C1.justification: The central claim that fine-detail reconstruction requires preserving some loss sharpness, and the claimed first investigation of sharpness and novel-view generalization, already appear in v1. v2 broadens the contribution explicitly beyond SAM to other flat-minima optimizers. NeRF and dynamic-scene applicability are retained claims, despite their stronger prominence in the revised framing.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive qualifications: the LoG implementation differs from the ideal tolerance definition, the geometric analysis primarily concerns Gaussian means, and unobserved regions can retain artifacts requiring additional priors. Appendix H discusses remaining tuning and limitations for non-geometric attributes in specular or transparent environments. The earlier emphasis on adversarial perturbation being essential gives way to a broader interpretation accommodating RWP.

D1.justification: The abstract changes the stated code status from a future release to available. v2 gives more explicit LoG scale-selection equations, reports the fixed mean-radius multiplier, and newly specifies 800 interpolated test views for Figure 1. Most baseline implementation instructions and the RTX A5000 timing disclosure are retained; external code availability was not independently checked.

R1.justification: v2 adds references supporting RWP, AnySplat, DTU, OMMO, and additional sparse-view/noise methods, including Seo et al.'s flat-minima work. Section 2.3 revises the relationship to random-noise methods by interpreting their success through loss flattening. The overall related-work organization and most research positioning remain intact.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, contribution statements, and conclusion are extensively rewritten around structure-aware sharpness. The method is reorganized into preliminaries, geometric tolerance, sharpness, and weighting, with expanded algorithmic exposition. Computational-cost discussion moves into the supplement, and the applications and appendix structure are substantially reorganized.

P2.justification: The document changes from two-column to single-column layout, with extensive figure and table restructuring. Figure 1 gains SAM and sharpness displays; the conceptual landscape illustration is replaced by a pixel-level example, and the old pipeline schematic disappears. Qualitative and ablation panels are rearranged, while new convergence, tolerance-map, robustness, and supplementary evaluation displays are added.

improvement.justification: v2 better substantiates and qualifies the retained central idea through the RWP experiment, sensitivity tests, an assumption-limited geometric derivation, and explicit failure cases. These improve explanatory support and applicability assessment without improving the retained benchmark scores. Some isolated controls disappear, and the added OMMO/DTU evaluations remain sparsely specified, tempering the overall gain.
